chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, despises a man who is entered upon in his house and does not fight (to defend it).
ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about defending one's home?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith emphasizes the principle of *hurmah* (sanctity) of the home, linking physical defense to personal dignity and social standing. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that passive acceptance of intrusion is not merely a lack of capability but a character flaw displeasing to Allah, underscoring the importance of asserting one's rights within the domestic sphere.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-24 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
The Honorable the Exalted God despises a man who does not defend his home when a stranger forcefully enters his house.”
